Product Vision: Waypoint Field Service Platform

Waypoint is a scheduling and dispatch platform for HVAC and plumbing contractors who send technicians into the field every day.

Field Technicians are the platform's most demanding stakeholders: they work out of a truck, often in basements or backyards with no signal, and they are the ones customers actually see.

Rising Customer Expectations for On-Time Arrival Windows is the driver behind this release. Customers increasingly expect a narrow, reliable arrival window instead of a vague "sometime this afternoon," and contractors that cannot deliver on that lose repeat business to competitors who can.

That driver motivates our top goal: Reduce Missed Service Appointments.

An internal review found that nearly a third of missed appointments trace to double-booked technicians, and that assessment is a major reason this goal is on the roadmap this quarter.

To reduce missed appointments, this goal aggregates one concrete requirement: an Offline-Capable Mobile Technician App. Field Technicians are the stakeholder most directly associated with this requirement, since they are the ones who lose the job the moment their signal drops.

The requirement is bounded by a hard constraint: Technicians Must Be Able to Complete Work Orders Without a Reliable Cellular Connection. Rural service routes and basement mechanical rooms routinely have no signal at all, so this constraint constrains exactly how the offline app requirement can be implemented -- data has to be captured locally and synced later, not streamed live.

We are guided by one principle above all: A Technician Should Never Need to Call Dispatch to Confirm a Job. Everything the technician needs -- the address, the access code, the customer's history -- should already be on the device. This principle realizes our top goal directly: fewer confirmation calls means fewer chances for a job to slip through the cracks.

Success here shows up as a specific outcome: Missed-Appointment Rate Cut in Half. That outcome is what actually realizes the goal -- the goal is the direction, the outcome is proof we got there.

Underneath all of this is a value we protect above almost anything else: Customer Trust. Every goal on this roadmap is, in the end, associated with preserving that value; a customer who has been stood up once rarely gives a contractor a third chance.

Finally, a note on Meaning: On-Time Means Arriving Within the Committed Appointment Window, Not Just the Same Day. That specific interpretation is associated with both the top goal and with Field Technicians, because a technician who shows up at 4:58 on a 3-5pm window has, by this definition, still met the goal -- arriving on the same day is not enough.
